results.name: between_set_yes_rate_sd
results.description: Standard deviation across number sets of each set's mean yes rate; observed > model means people treat some sets as far more (or less) generous than the model, i.e. the model under-produces set-level extremity (near-all-yes / near-all-no sets).

results.name: common_factor_rule_gap
results.description: Among multi-example sets whose examples all share a greatest common divisor g>=3, yes rate for targets divisible by g minus yes rate for targets not divisible by g; observed > model means people generalize the shared "multiples of g" rule more sharply than coherence-tuned pairwise factor similarity predicts.
results.code:
# name: common_factor_rule_gap
# description: Among multi-example sets whose examples all share a greatest common divisor g>=3, yes rate for targets divisible by g minus yes rate for targets not divisible by g; observed > model means people generalize the shared "multiples of g" rule more sharply than coherence-tuned pairwise factor similarity predicts.
def test_statistic(df):
    s = df["number_set"].astype(str)
    uniq = s.unique()
    gmap = {}
    for u in uniq:
        v = [int(z) for z in u.split(",")]
        g = 0
        for z in v:
            g = math.gcd(g, z)
        gmap[u] = g if (len(v) >= 2 and g >= 3) else 0
    g = s.map(gmap).values.astype(int)
    t = df["target"].astype(int).values
    y = df["rating"].astype(float).values
    m = g > 0
    if m.sum() == 0:
        return 0.0
    div = np.zeros(len(t), bool)
    div[m] = (t[m] % g[m]) == 0
    a = m & div
    b = m & ~div
    if a.sum() == 0 or b.sum() == 0:
        return 0.0
    return float(y[a].mean() - y[b].mean())

results.name: trial_index_drift
results.description: Pearson correlation between trial_index and the yes response; observed > model (model ~0, being stationary) means yes responses become more frequent later in the session.

results.name: parity_rule_gap_far
results.description: Among sets of 3-4 examples that all share parity but not a final digit, yes rate for same-parity targets minus opposite-parity targets, restricted to targets >5 from every example and sharing no final digit with any; observed > model means people extract an odd/even rule more strongly than coherence-stretched parity attention predicts (observed < model: the model over-weights parity).
results.code:
# name: parity_rule_gap_far
# description: Among sets of 3-4 examples that all share parity but not a final digit, yes rate for same-parity targets minus opposite-parity targets, restricted to targets >5 from every example and sharing no final digit with any; observed > model means people extract an odd/even rule more strongly than coherence-stretched parity attention predicts (observed < model: the model over-weights parity).
def test_statistic(df):
    s = df["number_set"].astype(str)
    ex = s.str.split(",", expand=True).reindex(columns=range(4))
    ex = ex.apply(pd.to_numeric, errors="coerce").values
    t = df["target"].astype(int).values
    y = df["rating"].astype(float).values
    valid = ~np.isnan(ex)
    k = valid.sum(1)
    e = np.nan_to_num(ex)
    par = np.where(valid, e % 2, np.nan)
    allpar = np.nanmax(par, 1) == np.nanmin(par, 1)
    dg = np.where(valid, e % 10, np.nan)
    alldig = np.nanmax(dg, 1) == np.nanmin(dg, 1)
    d = np.where(valid, np.abs(t[:, None] - ex), np.inf)
    match = (valid & (e % 10 == (t % 10)[:, None])).any(1)
    base = (k >= 3) & allpar & ~alldig & (d.min(1) > 5) & ~match
    same = (t % 2) == np.nanmin(par, 1)
    a = base & same
    b = base & ~same
    if a.sum() == 0 or b.sum() == 0:
        return 0.0
    return float(y[a].mean() - y[b].mean())

results.name: single_example_digit_vs_adjacent
results.description: For single-example sets, yes rate for distant (>10 away) targets sharing the example's final digit minus yes rate for adjacent (1-3 away) targets with a different final digit; observed > model means people weight a shared final digit over numeric closeness more than the model's baseline attention allows.
results.code:
# name: single_example_digit_vs_adjacent
# description: For single-example sets, yes rate for distant (>10 away) targets sharing the example's final digit minus yes rate for adjacent (1-3 away) targets with a different final digit; observed > model means people weight a shared final digit over numeric closeness more than the model's baseline attention allows.
def test_statistic(df):
    s = df["number_set"].astype(str)
    single = ~s.str.contains(",")
    x = pd.to_numeric(s.where(single, "0")).astype(int).values
    t = df["target"].astype(int).values
    y = df["rating"].astype(float).values
    d = np.abs(t - x)
    same = (t % 10) == (x % 10)
    sm = single.values
    a = sm & same & (d > 10)
    b = sm & (~same) & (d >= 1) & (d <= 3)
    if a.sum() == 0 or b.sum() == 0:
        return 0.0
    return float(y[a].mean() - y[b].mean())

results.name: adjacent_nonmember_yes_rate
results.description: Among multi-example sets, yes rate for targets not in the set that lie within 3 of some example but share no final digit with any example; observed < model means the model over-generalizes by numeric closeness to near neighbours.
results.code:
# name: adjacent_nonmember_yes_rate
# description: Among multi-example sets, yes rate for targets not in the set that lie within 3 of some example but share no final digit with any example; observed < model means the model over-generalizes by numeric closeness to near neighbours.
def test_statistic(df):
    s = df["number_set"].astype(str)
    ex = s.str.split(",", expand=True).reindex(columns=range(4))
    ex = ex.apply(pd.to_numeric, errors="coerce").values
    t = df["target"].astype(int).values[:, None]
    y = df["rating"].astype(float).values
    valid = ~np.isnan(ex)
    multi = valid.sum(1) >= 2
    d = np.where(valid, np.abs(t - ex), np.inf)
    inset = (d == 0).any(1)
    near = (d <= 3).any(1)
    digit = (valid & (np.nan_to_num(ex) % 10 == t % 10)).any(1)
    m = multi & ~inset & near & ~digit
    if m.sum() == 0:
        return 0.0
    return float(y[m].mean())

results.name: small_vs_large_magnitude_near_gap
results.description: Among non-member targets 4-15 away from their nearest example and sharing no final digit with any example, yes rate when the nearest example is >=50 minus when it is <=25; observed > model means similarity in size is log-like (Weber) — a fixed absolute gap counts as closer among large numbers — which the model's linear magnitude metric misses.
results.code:
# name: small_vs_large_magnitude_near_gap
# description: Among non-member targets 4-15 away from their nearest example and sharing no final digit with any example, yes rate when the nearest example is >=50 minus when it is <=25; observed > model means similarity in size is log-like (Weber) — a fixed absolute gap counts as closer among large numbers — which the model's linear magnitude metric misses.
def test_statistic(df):
    s = df["number_set"].astype(str)
    ex = s.str.split(",", expand=True).reindex(columns=range(4))
    ex = ex.apply(pd.to_numeric, errors="coerce").values
    t = df["target"].astype(int).values
    y = df["rating"].astype(float).values
    valid = ~np.isnan(ex)
    d = np.where(valid, np.abs(t[:, None] - ex), np.inf)
    j = d.argmin(1)
    dn = d[np.arange(len(t)), j]
    xn = ex[np.arange(len(t)), j]
    digit = (valid & (np.nan_to_num(ex) % 10 == (t % 10)[:, None])).any(1)
    base = (dn >= 4) & (dn <= 15) & ~digit
    a = base & (xn >= 50)
    b = base & (xn <= 25)
    if a.sum() == 0 or b.sum() == 0:
        return 0.0
    return float(y[a].mean() - y[b].mean())

results.name: far_single_digit_match_multi
results.description: Among multi-example sets whose examples do not all share a final digit, yes rate for targets >10 away from every example that share a final digit with at least one example, minus yes rate for targets >10 away sharing no final digit with any example; observed > model means a single example's final digit drives generalization more than the model's recency-weighted, untuned digit attention predicts.
results.code:
# name: far_single_digit_match_multi
# description: Among multi-example sets whose examples do not all share a final digit, yes rate for targets >10 away from every example that share a final digit with at least one example, minus yes rate for targets >10 away sharing no final digit with any example; observed > model means a single example's final digit drives generalization more than the model's recency-weighted, untuned digit attention predicts.
def test_statistic(df):
    s = df["number_set"].astype(str)
    ex = s.str.split(",", expand=True).reindex(columns=range(4))
    ex = ex.apply(pd.to_numeric, errors="coerce").values
    t = df["target"].astype(int).values
    y = df["rating"].astype(float).values
    valid = ~np.isnan(ex)
    k = valid.sum(1)
    dig = np.where(valid, np.nan_to_num(ex) % 10, -1)
    nd = np.where(valid, dig, np.nan)
    allsame = (np.nanmax(nd, 1) == np.nanmin(nd, 1))
    d = np.where(valid, np.abs(t[:, None] - ex), np.inf)
    far = d.min(1) > 10
    match = (valid & (dig == (t % 10)[:, None])).any(1)
    base = (k >= 2) & ~allsame & far
    a = base & match
    b = base & ~match
    if a.sum() == 0 or b.sum() == 0:
        return 0.0
    return float(y[a].mean() - y[b].mean())
